ORAL JUDGMENT (PER: THE HON'BLE DR. JUSTICE CHILLAKUR SUMALATHA) Heard Sri G.R.Turamari, learned counsel for the appellants as well as Sri R.R.Mane learned counsel for respondent No.2.
No representation for respondent No.1 on call.

2. Challenge in this appeal is the order that is rendered by the Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Saundatti, (hereinafter be referred to as "the Tribunal" for brevity) in MVC No.225/2012 dated 13.03.2014.

entities.text: Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Saundatti
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: This is a claimants' appeal.

3. The matrix of the case as projected by the appellants before the Tribunal is that, the deceased Kashappa (hereinafter be referred to as "the deceased"
for brevity) went to Munavalli Shandy for purchase of sheep on 13.05.2010.
He was waiting for bus near Panchalingeshwar Cross at Munavalli.
At that time, a truck bearing registration No.KA-22/D-2972 came from NC: 2025:KHC-D:13648 HC-KAR Yadagiri side.
The deceased was boarding the said truck and in the meantime, the driver of the truck drove the vehicle, due to which the deceased fell down and the wheel of the truck ran over his right foot.
Thereby the deceased sustained grievous injuries.
The deceased filed a petition claiming compensation and during the pendency of the claim petition he died.

4. Subjecting the evidence of PW1, Exs.P1 to P.13 and Ex.R1 to scrutiny, the Tribunal came to a conclusion that the claimants are entitled to a sum of 99,400/- as compensation and that the said amount is liable to be paid by respondent No.1 i.e., the owner of the offending vehicle.
5. Arguing the matter, learned counsel for the appellants submits that the Tribunal unjustifiably exonerated respondent No.2-Insurance Company from the liability.

Learned counsel states that, as the deceased met with an accident while he was boarding the truck in NC: 2025:KHC-D:13648 HC-KAR question and as the said truck was insured with the 2nd respondent, the 2nd respondent is equally liable to pay compensation to the appellants/claimants.
6.

The submission that is made by learned counsel for respondent No.2 on the other hand is that,
the deceased was an unauthorized passenger and the terms and conditions of the policy does not cover the risk of said unauthorized passenger and therefore, the Tribunal rightly exonerated the Insurance Company i.e., respondent No.2 from the liability to pay compensation.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In reply to the said submission, learned counsel for the appellants submits that the Tribunal at least should have ordered pay and recovery.
8. There is no material on record to show that the risk of the deceased was covered under the terms and conditions of the policy.
However, the fact remains is that due to the involvement of the vehicle which is insured NC: 2025:KHC-D:13648 HC-KAR with respondent No.2, the accident occurred and the deceased sustained injuries.
Therefore, as rightly contended, the Tribunal ought to have ordered pay and recovery.

Therefore, this Court considers desirable to dispose of the appeal with a direction to respondent No.2/ Insurance Company to pay the amount that was awarded as compensation to the appellants/claimants and thereafter to recover the same from the owner of the vehicle i.e.,
respondent No.1 herein.

9. Therefore the following;
 ORDER  i) The appeal is allowed in part.

ii) Respondent No.2/Insurance Company is directed to pay the amount that is awarded as compensation by the Tribunal to the appellants/claimants along with interest within a period of 8 weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment.
NC: 2025:KHC-D:13648 HC-KAR iii) On deposit, respondent No.2 is permitted to recover the deposited amount from respondent No.1 as per the procedure established by law.

Sd/-
